simple.meaning: רָקָב (râqâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “decay (by caries).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רָקָב (H7538) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 13:28, with occurrences in Job, Proverbs, Hosea, Habakkuk.

simple.summary: רָקָב (râqâb) / H7538 is traced through Job 13:28, Proverbs 12:4, Proverbs 14:30, Hosea 5:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7538. raqab רָקָב noun [masculine] rottenness, decay (always figurative); — ׳ר absolute; apparently of ravages of worm, in יְהוּדָה בֵּית , in figure Hosea 5:12 (|| עָשׁ ), compare Job 13:28 (|| id. ); elsewhere of decay of bones, caries (in figurative), ׳ר ׳בְּעַצְמ Hab 3:16 ; Prov 12:4 , construct עַצְמ ׳רְקֵב 14:30 .

occurrences.englishText: though I am decaying like a rotten thing,
A worthy woman is the crown of her husband,
The life of the body is a heart at peace,
Therefore I am to Ephraim like a moth,
I heard, and my body trembled.
